articles.title: Solaris Energy Co-CEO on Data Center Power Demand and Energy Infrastructure Growth
articles.summary:
At the opening of NYSE Texas in Dallas, Amanda Brock, Co-CEO of Solaris Energy Infrastructure, joined NYSE Live to discuss the rapidly evolving energy landscape and the growing demand for infrastructure supporting AI and data center growth.

Brocl explains that Solaris is focused on delivering power infrastructure and energy solutions to customers facing increasing electricity requirements. As artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and data center development accelerate, the company is working to help organizations secure reliable power amid growing constraints on the electric grid.
A significant portion of the interview focuses on the connection between energy infrastructure and AI-driven demand.
 
Brock discusses how hyperscalers, cloud providers, technology companies, and data center operators are seeking faster access to power as computing requirements continue to expand. She explains why speed-to-compute has become a critical priority across the industry.

The conversation also explores Solaris' role in delivering behind-the-meter power solutions and microgrid infrastructure. Brock discusses how the company helps customers navigate grid limitations while supporting power generation, distribution, and delivery requirements for large-scale projects.

Another major theme is the company's expansion into integrated infrastructure services. Brock explains how Solaris has broadened its capabilities beyond temporary power solutions and now participates across multiple stages of the power delivery process, including fuel sourcing, generation, electrical infrastructure, and on-site deployment.
The interview further examines Solaris' acquisition strategy. Brock discusses recent transactions aimed at strengthening the company's operational capabilities and supporting greater vertical integration. She explains that acquisitions are helping Solaris expand the range of services it can provide while responding quickly to a rapidly growing market.
Additionally, Brock shares her perspective on the significance of NYSE Texas and Solaris' decision to become dual listed. She highlights the company's strong Texas roots and discusses the importance of supporting innovation, investment, and infrastructure development across the state.
Throughout the discussion, Brock provides insights into energy infrastructure, AI-driven power demand, data center growth, grid constraints, microgrids, strategic acquisitions, natural gas-powered solutions, and the long-term outlook for the sector.
